contract_answer.question: Does increasing degradation-law rho from 0.5 to 1.0 reduce held-out law-fit excess over the true-EOL floor by at least 30% while keeping split-2021 MAPE at or below 0.1049 and avoiding BALANCE_FAIL?
contract_answer.conclusion: Reviewer recomputation from all 600 selected-checkpoint predictions confirms best epoch 5 of 11, MAPE 0.090828, Acc@15 0.886667, RMSE 20.3528 cycles, bias -9.7554 cycles, and prediction/target spread 0.76538. The parent NA-E009 values are 0.099874, 0.743333, 22.5282, -15.9075, and 0.74972, so MAPE improves by 0.00905, Acc@15 by 0.14333, and RMSE by 2.18 cycles. Prefix-band MAPE is 0.1588/0.0840/0.0849/0.0786/0.0859 versus 0.1221/0.0936/0.0928/0.0932/0.1085. Balance passes at calibrated lambda 0.178031 with median R 1.156 and cosine +0.577 then +0.975. However, held-out law-fit error is 0.0385 versus parent 0.0463 and floor 0.0161: excess falls 25.8%, short of the registered 30% rule and its error cutoff of 0.0372 by 0.0013. The pre-registered rule therefore requires DISCARD despite the meaningful accuracy gain.

The schema gradient gate is FAIL because diagnostics.json overall_gradient_health is UNHEALTHY: its legacy physics summary flags R above 1 and a loss-value ratio above 1, while the governing loss.md 5.3 balance gate explicitly uses R in [0.05, 2.0] and says loss value is not a gate. loss_balance therefore passes at median R 1.156; all gradients are finite, the law head and encoder update, and padding is invariant, so the run remains VALID.

next_action.summary: Close the degradation-law direction and retain the frozen NA-E009 configuration. NA-E026 is a promising accuracy result, but its one registered rho repair still misses the defining law-fit cutoff by 0.0013. Confirming it on splits 42 and 2024 after that miss would replace the pre-registered physics gate with a post-hoc accuracy gate; do not move the goalposts.
